entertainment.body:
IATSE Local One, which represents stagehands on Broadway , has reached a tentative agreement with the Broadway League, ahead of the lucrative holiday weeks.

This comes after Local One members had voted to authorize a strike in October, after working on an expired contract since late July. If called, a work stoppage from Local One would have likely put a halt to most Broadway shows. The agreement still needs to be ratified by members of the union, with details of the tentative agreement planned to be available ahead of the union’s December meeting.

However, another local chapter of the union, IATSE Local 764, which represents Broadway dressers and others who work on costumes, still remains without a contract, and voted Sunday to authorize a strike if necessary.

Local 764 members have been bargaining with The Broadway League, a trade association for Broadway producers and general managers, since June. The members’ previous agreement had expired July 26. The League cancelled bargaining sessions scheduled for November 18 and 19, according to IATSE, and Local 764 has been pushing for new dates.

IATSE said the issues still in contention include wages and a gender pay gap that has existed for decades for Broadway wardrobe workers. The field is predominantly female, and has been paid “significantly lower rates than stagehand classifications historically held predominantly by men” according to the union, with Local 764 department heads needing to work 45 percent longer to earn pay comparable to workers in similar department-head roles.

Both Actors’ Equity and the American Federation of Musicians Local 802 also voted to authorize strikes last year, and came very close to doing so, before striking new contracts with the Broadway League.

entertainment.title: Reclusive actor Jack Nicholson’s son reveals surprising way his dad launched his legendary Hollywood career
entertainment.summary: The three-time Oscar winner is now rarely seen publicly.
entertainment.body:
Jack Nicholson launched his prolific acting career purely by chance.

The legendary thespian’s son Ray Nicholson revealed his dad became an actor when he connected with his agent through their sweet tooth.

“My dad served in the [Air National Guard], and that’s where he met his agent, Sandy Bresler,” Ray told People in an interview published Tuesday.

“He didn’t do anything, but they both liked sweets, so that’s how they met each other and started a legendary career,” he continued.

Jack, 89, served in the California National Air Guard from 1957 to 1962.

He made his film debut in the 1958 thriller “The Cry Baby Killer” while serving in the Guard.

Want more celebrity and pop culture news? Start your day with Page Six Daily.

Bresler served as Jack’s agent for 60 years, before he died in 2024 at age 87.

entertainment.title: Rylee Arnold sobs over ‘DWTS’ partner Connor Wood’s ‘thoughtful and meaningful’ gift ahead of finale
entertainment.summary: The pro dancer was shocked when she opened Wood's gift.
entertainment.body:
Rylee Arnold broke down in tears in an Instagram video shared ahead of Tuesday’s “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 finale, after opening what she called “the most thoughtful and meaningful” gift from her celebrity partner, Connor Wood .

“Stop it!” the 21-year-old exclaimed as she lifted the lid on a gray box to reveal the Rapunzel dress she wore during Week 8’s “Disney Night.”

“You guys, he bought my Rapunzel dress,” Arnold said through tears. “We don’t get to keep our costumes, ever.”

Arnold gushed over the “perfect” gift, explaining that she’s “never been able to keep a costume in [her] life.”

When Wood walked into the room, he confirmed that he bought the dress from the show’s costume department, though it’s unclear what rate they offered for the floral purple ensemble.

Arnold — who joined “DWTS” as a pro dancer in 2023 — wore Rapunzel’s fanciful lavender dress, while Wood cosplayed as Flynn Rider for their Waltz to “I See the Light” from Disney’s “Tangled” movie.

The pair earned a 32 out of 40 score from the judges, with guest judge Cynthia Erivo praising their “commitment to storytelling.”

In a post-show interview with “Good Morning America,” Arnold said it has always been her dream to bring Rapunzel to life in the “DWTS” ballroom.

entertainment.title: Broadway Box Office: ‘Hamilton’ Rises Back Up to $3M, ‘Here There are Blueberries’ Cracks $1M
entertainment.summary: 'Inter Alia,' starring Rosamund Pike, is also continuing to build momentum.
entertainment.body:
Hamilton was the top grossing show last week, rising back above $3 million as the industry neared its lucrative holiday week, followed by Other Desert Cities with $2.5 million and the Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell-led Much Ado About Nothing , which still brought in $2 million in a week that included its comped opening night performance.

The Lion King followed with $1.9 million and Harry Potter and the Cursed Child with $1.7 million.

Inter Alia, starring Rosamund Pike, continues to build momentum, bringing in close to $1 million ($993,103) with 100 percent capacity, across its first week of seven performances. The play is set to open Dec. 1.

Here There are Blueberries , a play about museum curators examining previously undiscovered photos from the Holocaust, cracked $1 million for the first time since beginning previews in early November. The show played to close to 100 percent capacity with an average ticket price of $128.

New musical Galileo saw a slight dip in capacity and grosses after lead actor Raúl Esparza missed performances from Nov. 16 through Nov. 18 while recovering from a concussion. The show brought in $699,975 across six performances, and saw capacity fall to 92 percent. The musical is scheduled to open Dec. 6.

Wanted, a new musical which opened Nov. 8, also saw a dip in capacity down to 85 percent, with the show grossing $661,143 across eight performances.

Broadway’s holiday fare has not yet taken off with consumers, with The Blue Man Group playing to 60 percent capacity, illusionist show Now You See Me playing to 77 percent capacity and radio play It’s a Wonderful Life playing to 76 percent.

sports.title: Thanksgiving week features extra episodes of #PFTPM
sports.summary: Thanksgiving week typically alters the usual PFT Live schedule.
sports.body:
Like every year, PFT Live shuts down on Thanksgiving and Black Friday. After weeks of five two-hour shows every Monday through Friday, the crew deserves a break on the two days that most of the rest of the world takes a break.

Enter #PFTPM. If you’ve noticed (or if you haven’t), we’ve significantly increased #PFTPM this season. It’s a YouTube exclusive, with some of the clips landing in PFT posts.

This week, new #PFTPM episodes will land on Wednesday afternoon (the usual weekly nuggets episode), on Friday (a review of the three Thanksgiving games plus anything else of interest), the usual Saturday episode, and the pair of Sunday editions reviewing the early afternoon and late afternoon windows.

We’ll also be trying something new. With the NFL staging a Thanksgiving Eve game for the first time (Packers-Rams), I’ll be taping a reaction to the game immediately after it ends at or about 11:30 p.m. ET.

If nothing else, it will keep me from consuming excessive amounts of adult beverages during the game. Or not, which will make the episode even more interesting.

sports.title: Report: NFL, YouTube are negotiating a three-game package for 2027
sports.summary: YouTube's on-again, off-again arrangements to stream select NFL games may be on again.
sports.body:
This year, Christmas Eve lands on a Thursday; Prime Video will televise the Texans-Eagles game that night (barring a flex). Next year, Christmas Eve lands on a Friday.

YouTube was at one point negotiating the five-game package for 2026 that landed with Netflix. It includes Wednesday night’s first-of-its-kind Thanksgiving Eve game between the Packers and Rams. YouTube walked, as Ourand reported at the time, when the league tried to split the five-game package between multiple partners.

The arrangement between the NFL and YouTube currently includes Sunday Ticket. That package could be disappearing in the next round of broadcast deals.

The inevitable expansion of the regular season to 18 games per team will create another 16 games that can be sliced and diced into special packages.

sports.title: Brandon Aiyuk will visit Commanders
sports.summary: Aiyuk has mentioned signing with Washington for months.
sports.body:
The former 49ers receiver cleared waivers on Tuesday. Agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN that Aiyuk is scheduled to visit the Commanders on Wednesday.

Aiyuk has been linked to the Commanders for months. He played college football at Arizona State with quarterback Jayden Daniels. Commanders G.M. Adam Peters worked for the 49ers when Aiyuk arrived as a first-round pick in 2020.

And the Commanders — a sudden contender in the NFC East — could use some help at the position.

Aiyuk has been vocal about his desire to play for the Commanders. It got a little dicey during Aiyuk’s social-media tirade over the summer; a couple of his attacks were targeted at Daniels.

Regardless, the Commanders will be getting the first crack at Aiyuk, who is extra motivated to sign a contract and to start playing, especially after the 49ers delayed his free agency for two weeks after he was reinstated by the league from the reserve/left squad list.

sports.body: Week 12 is going to be a wild one. Weather alerts are already out there. Practice schedules are already skewed. And injury reports are just educated guesses at this point. The Buffalo Bills will host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, but as they prepare for a game that could determine when – and where – they will play in January, they haven’t had a full practice this week. After no practice Monday, they held a walk-through practice today, which means injury reports are estimates. Good estimates, made by qualified medical staff, but estimates just the same. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2125349727147569363?a=WEkmDC-gFJQugxMZIXU&s=20] With that in mind, we’re going to look at who we think is trending toward playing versus who can probably safely eat an early Thanksgiving meal on Thursday. Bills Players Trending Up * S Cole Bishop * T Spencer Brown * S Damar Hamlin * TE Jackson Hawes * S Amani Hooker * RB Ty Johnson * C Connor McGovern * DL Ed Oliver * OLB Greg Rousseau * DL T.J. Sanders Of these players listed above, only Sanders was estimated to not practice in full. Good news for Brown, Hamlin and Rousseau who were limited on Monday. I would expect that all of these should be ready to play Thursday. Bills Players Holding Steady * CB Christian Benford * TE Dalton Kincaid * G O’Cyrus Torrence * LB Dorian Williams Everyone was limited – which is great news for Benford who hasn’t practiced in over a week. I would still expect Benford and Williams to be questionable. But, still, I wouldn’t be surprised if the Bills’ inactive list is full of “healthy” scratches Thursday night. ______________________ The Chiefs are dealing with a tight schedule as well – plus have a travel day built in. sports.title: Bears add CB Isaac Yiadom off waivers
sports.summary: The Bears have added a defensive back.
sports.body:
Chicago has claimed cornerback Isaac Yiadom off waivers, the team announced on Tuesday.

The cornerback appeared in three games for the Commanders this season, playing exclusively on special teams.

Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has plenty of familiarity with Yiadom, as the cornerback played under him when Allen was New Orleans’ head coach in 2022 and 2023.

A Broncos third-round pick in 2018, Yiadom has played 121 career games with 34 starts for the Broncos, Giants, Packers, Texans, Saints, 49ers, and Commanders.

sports.title: Michigan does about-face on Trev Alberts, potentially owing him $17.2 million
sports.summary: The last time Trev Alberts made this kind of a stir, he was the subject of Bill Tobin's legendary rant against Mel Kiper.
sports.body:
This time, the situation potentially involves a significant payment to Alberts.

Via ESPN, Michigan backed out of an agreement to hire Alberts (who played in only 29 career games over three seasons after being the fifth overall pick in the 1994 draft) to become the university’s next athletic director. Alberts told ESPN that he had signed a “binding memorandum of understanding” for the position.

Alberts’s lawyer, Tom Mars, told ESPN that Michigan owes Alberts a $17.2 million buyout.

For that kind of money, Michigan will be very tempted to refuse to pay, forcing litigation and the expense, uncertainty, and delay that goes along with it. Alberts could decide to take less than he’s owed, simply to end the fight.

Of course, Alberts also could become determined to prove a point — if he and Mars believe Alberts has an ironclad claim to the money.

Michigan’s about-face apparently relates to deposition testimony from Alberts in a Title IX case arising from his tenure at Nebraska. Per ESPN, Alberts gave testimony on December 4, 2025, that Michigan regards as problematic.

Alberts was asked whether he believes it’s true that college coaches should never have sex with the athletes they’re coaching. The obvious answer is, “Yes.” Alberts pursued a different strategy.

He then said the situation could be “nuanced,” due to preexisting relationships or eligibility waivers that could result in athletes being nearly the same age as young assistant coaches.

sports.title: Giants put Greg Newsome on injured reserve
sports.summary: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday that cornerback Greg Newsome will miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain and a clearer picture of just how many weeks came on Tuesday.
sports.body:
Newsome was placed on the injured reserve list, which means he’ll be out for at least the next four games. Newsome signed a one-year deal with the Giants in the offseason and signed a three-year extension earlier this month.

Paulson Adebo is expected to see more playing time with Newsome out of the lineup.

The Giants filled Newsome’s roster spot by signing linebacker Dawuane Smoot off of the practice squad. He has appeared in three games and had three tackles and a sack in those appearances.

sports.title: Player-turned-doctor Laurent Duvernay-Tardif is working with the Chiefs' medical staff
sports.summary: Former Chiefs offensive lineman Laurent Duvernay-Tardif, who got his medical degree while playing in the NFL, is back in Kansas City working with the Chiefs' medical staff.
sports.body:
“Feeling privileged to be back on the sidelines, this time shadowing the medical team to gain experience in sports medicine and on-field emergency response,” Duvernay-Tardif wrote on social media.

A native of Quebec who has been completing medical training there since retiring from the NFL, Duvernay-Tardif is currently spending a month with the Chiefs’ medical staff to learn more about treatment of athletes.

Listed at 6-foot-5 and 321 pounds during his playing days, Duvernay-Tardif appears to have lost weight and blended in on the sideline during Sunday’s Chiefs game, although CBS briefly showed him on camera.

Duvernay-Tardif was a starter for the Chiefs from 2015 to 2019. He chose not to play in 2020, instead lending his medical expertise to covid patients. He returned and played for the Jets in 2021 and 2022.

sports.title: Sean Payton suspends J.K. Dobbins for Week 12 for conduct detrimental to the team
sports.summary: Dobbins played just one offensive snap in the Week 11 win over the Raiders.
sports.body:
Head coach Sean Payton announced in his Tuesday press conference that Dobbins has been suspended one game for conduct detrimental to the team.

Payton did not elaborate or answer any follow-up questions, though he did note that the suspension was his decision.

Dobbins began the season as Denver’s starting running back but has now filled that role in just one of the last four games, with rookie Jonah Coleman taking over as the Broncos’ lead back.

Coleman rushed for 111 yards on 24 carries with three touchdowns and caught four passes for 18 yards in Sunday’s victory over the Raiders.

Dobbins was on the field for just one offensive snap in Week 11, taking a carry that was stuffed for no gain.

In 10 games with seven starts this season, Dobbins has rushed for 324 yards with three touchdowns and caught nine passes for 31 yards.

sports.title: Brandon Aiyuk is a free agent after clearing waivers
sports.summary: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is officially a free agent.
sports.body:
Aiyuk went unclaimed around the league after the 49ers placed him on waivers Monday, which means that he’s now free to sign a contract with any club. It was the expected result as any team claiming Aiyuk would also inherit his contract.

Aiyuk expressed interest in signing with the Commanders during his extended impasse with the 49ers and the path is now clear for that to happen. Given how long Aiyuk has been off of the field, it would seem likely that his stint with his next team will begin on the practice squad.

There’s no word about a deal at this point, but things can develop quickly now that Aiyuk is free to sign.

sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills suddenly have two vacant spots on their practice squad. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills suddenly have two vacant spots on their practice squad. Core pieces of said practice squad, quarterback Shane Buechele and 2025 sixth-round pick Chase Lundt, were added to the 53-man rosters of other teams in separate transactions on Tuesday before the club’s Week 12 Thanksgiving contest against the Chiefs. First it was Buechele: [Media: https://twitter.com/AdamSchefter/status/2125319223455215868?a=k48cEgeesAAWtA1pZGk&s=20] Given the Colts released Daniel Jones on November 20, they were in need of more quarterback depth behind former first-rounder Anthony Richardson, who’s become the team’s starter. Buechle is presumed to be Indianapolis’ new No. 3 quarterback behind Richardson and Riley Leonard. Buechele spent from 2023 - 2025 with the Bills before re-signing in Buffalo in January 2026. Under 20 minutes later, it was reported that Lundt was on the move too: [Media: https://twitter.com/TomPelissero/status/2125323896421511186?a=4r4MJdm1Jq7U7WwUMwc&s=20] The Seahawks are dealing with injuries to newly acquired guard Quenton Nelson, longtime right tackle Abraham Lucas, and franchise left tackle Charles Cross. The former sixth-round pick failed to appear in a regular-season game for the Bills but played over 300 preseason snaps the past two summers after a collegiate career at UConn. Who do you think the Bills should add to their practice squad after losing Buechele and Lundt?

sports.title: Kenneth Walker limited in his return to Chiefs practice
sports.summary: Walker missed the last two games with a groin injury.
sports.body:
Walker has missed the last two games with a groin injury, but his return to work would seem to open the door to a return to the lineup against the Bills on Thursday night.

Walker ran 159 times for 872 yards and seven touchdowns in eight games before the injury. He also has 26 catches for 172 yards and four touchdowns.

Tight end Noah Gray also returned to practice which left right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) was the only Chief out of practice. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was listed as limited while Gray (rib), cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder), wide receiver Rashee Rice (knee), right guard Trey Smith (concussion), and defensive lineman Peter Woods (neck) were full participants.

sports.title: Panthers do not activate Brady Christensen at expiration of 21-day practice window
sports.summary: As it turns out, the Panthers will not have one of their offensive linemen return for the 2026 season.
sports.body:
Via Alex Zietlow of the Charlotte Observer , Carolina did not activate offensive lineman Brady Christensen to the 53-man roster, allowing his 21-day practice window to expire.

That means Christensen will revert to being on injured reserve and is ineligible to return to the team’s roster in 2026.

Christensen suffered a hamstring injury in August after suffering a torn Achilles in the middle of the 2025 season.

A Panthers third-round pick in 2021, Christensen has appeared in 59 career games with 34 starts.

sports.title: Jake Ferguson, Tyler Booker remain out of practice for Cowboys
sports.summary: The Cowboys upgraded the practice participation of a couple of players on Tuesday's injury report, but two offensive starters remained out.
sports.body:
Right guard Tyler Booker (ankle) and tight end Jake Ferguson (knee, ankle) were listed as non-participants for the second straight day. Ferguson has missed the last two games and Booker was out against the Titans last Sunday, so it seems unlikely either will play against the Eagles on Thanksgiving.

Linebackers Jaishawn Barham (hip, groin) and Dee Winters (knee) both returned as limited participants. Barham did not play against the Titans, but Winters had two tackles.

Wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle) was downgraded to out and safety P.J. Locke (concussion) was limited for the second straight day. Cornerback Cobie Durant (neck), linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle), cornerback Devin Moore (hip), defensive tackle Otito Ogbonnia (knee), cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (foot), quarterback Dak Prescott (left hand), and safety Jalen Thompson (hamstring) remained full participants.

sports.title: Eagles sign LB Chance Campbell, waive C Jake Majors
sports.summary: The Eagles made a couple of changes to their roster ahead of Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
sports.body:
The team announced that they have signed linebacker Chance Campbell off of their practice squad. They waived center Jake Majors in a corresponding move.

Campbell has appeared in one game this season. He played 11 special teams snaps and made one tackle in Week 3. Campbell also played in four games for the Titans during the 2023 season.

Majors started two games earlier this season while the Eagles were dealing with a number of injuries on the offensive line. Drew Kendall is now handling center duties for the Eagles.

sports.title: Seahawks add Chase Lundt off Bills practice squad, waive CB Avery Smith
sports.summary: The Seahawks are making a pair of roster moves on Tuesday.
sports.body:
Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, Seattle is signing offensive tackle Chase Lundt off of Buffalo’s practice squad.

As a corresponding roster move, the team is waiving cornerback Avery Smith.

Lundt, 26, was a sixth-round pick in 2025. He’s appeared in two career games, playing three offensive snaps and five special teams snaps.

Smith appeared in six games for Seattle this season, playing exclusively on special teams.

sports.body: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. The Buffalo Bills remain in control of their playoff fate thanks to an AFC-best 9-1 record. Buffalo has been able to meet almost every challenge thrown its way during the team’s current six-game win streak. An early concern, the Bills’ defense has demanded respect around the league in recent weeks thanks to allowing zero touchdowns in three consecutive games while surrendering just nine field goals. Since their bye in Week 7, Buffalo has given up just one touchdown (to running back Derrick Henry of the Baltimore Ravens). There has been plenty of discussion about the quality of quarterbacks the Bills have faced in the last month, but it’s impossible to ignore the defensive turnaround post bye. In their first six games, Buffalo’s defense allowed 171 points, giving up an average of 28.5 for last in the NFL in scoring defense. In the four games since the bye, that figure has plummeted to 37 points — an average of 9.3 points per game. For all those saying the Bills have had an easy road, the same can be said of the Chiefs who haven’t defeated a team over .500 since Week 1. One thing’s clear: It gets much tougher for both teams on the road ahead, starting against one another in Week 12. Quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes bring out the best in each other, and they get to renew their friendship during primetime in front of a holiday audience. This time, however, both teams will have a potent rushing attack to lean on. That means we could see running backs James Cook III and either Kenneth Walker III or rookie Emmett Johnson take featured roles in the game’s outcome. Bills Mafia knows how great Allen and Cook are, and that when both are producing it’s almost impossible to stop Buffalo’s offense. sports.title: Dan Quinn on Stefon Diggs: I love his fire
sports.summary: Monday night ended well for the Commanders, but the start of the game was rough for the team's offense and frustrations about that boiled over on the sideline at one point.
sports.body:
Wide receiver Stefon Diggs was caught by ESPN cameras yelling in the direction of quarterback Jayden Daniels and lip readers shared that he appeared to be telling him to “throw the f—-king ball” after a sack ended a Washington drive in the second quarter. The Commanders bounced back with a touchdown the next time they got the ball and wound up with a 22-20 win on a last-second field goal.

The result made it easier to gloss over any bad feelings that cropped up earlier in the evening and head coach Dan Quinn said on Tuesday that he has no issue with Diggs using his voice in that manner.

“I love his fire , I do,” Quinn said, via John Keim of ESPN.com. “I love that. There’s a lot of good that comes with it where it can sound like he’s mad but it’s like some energy that comes behind it.”

Quinn added that “if something didn’t feel right I would step in and address it,” but that the current mindset in Washington appears to be all’s well that ends well.

sports.title: Titans have only defense in the NFL giving up scores on most of its drives
sports.summary: The Titans' defense allowed the Cowboys' offense to score on every drive on Sunday, with the exception of a kneeldown at the end of the game.
sports.body:
Tennessee’s defense has now given up a score on 50.5 percent of opposing possessions this season. The Titans are the only defense in the league that gives up points most of the time it takes the field.

Over the last two games, the Titans’ defense went on an incredible run: In addition to giving up scores on the Cowboys’ first eight offensive possessions in Week 11, the Titans gave up points on the Jaguars’ last five possessions in Week 10. That streak of 13 consecutive drives giving up scores is the longest streak of consecutive drives in which any NFL defense has given up points, for as far back as full drive data is available.

The Titans’ defense’s last 14 drives ended in 10 touchdowns, three field goals and a kneeldown.

Titans coach Robert Saleh has had success as a defensive coordinator, but he went 20-36 in his previous stint as head coach of the Jets, and he’s now 1-9 with the Titans. When he’s the head coach, his defenses don’t get the job done.

sports.title: Colts sign QB Shane Buechele off Bills practice squad
sports.summary: The Colts have added a third quarterback to their active roster.
sports.body:
The team announced on Tuesday that they have signed Shane Buechele off of the Bills’ practice squad. He will slot in as the third quarterback in Indianapolis behind Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard.

Buechele has been with the Bills for most of the last four seasons, but he did have a brief stint on the Chiefs’ roster after Patrick Mahomes was injured last year. He made his regular season debut for Kansas City during that stint and went 7-of-14 for 88 yards in Week 18.

The Colts also announced that they have signed veteran defensive end Carl Lawson off of their practice squad. They placed defensive end Caden Curry on injured reserve and waived offensive tackle Charlie Heck in corresponding moves.

sports.title: Ravens waive returner LaJohntay Wester
sports.summary: After he had a rough Sunday in Charlotte, the Ravens are moving on from LaJohntay Wester.
sports.body:
Per Jeff Zrebiec of TheAthletic.com, Baltimore has waived Wester on Wednesday.

Wester muffed a pair of punts in the loss to the Panthers, with Carolina recovering one of them.

A sixth-round pick in last year’s draft, Wester averaged 8.2 yards per punt return and 23.7 yards per kick return in 11 games this season. He averaged 12.4 yards per punt return and 24.6 yards per kick return in 2025.

Wester also contributed five catches for 58 yards in 2026. But with four fumbles this season and three in the last three games, Baltimore has elected to move on.

sports.title: Chiefs sign OT Fred Johnson to 53-man roster
sports.summary: The Chiefs announced a pair of roster moves on Tuesday afternoon.
sports.body:
They have signed offensive tackle Fred Johnson to their 53-man roster from the practice squad. Fullback Ben VanSumeren was placed on injured reserve in a corresponding move.

Johnson was released by the Eagles earlier this month and he signed to the practice squad in Kansas City last week. He played in seven games for the Eagles this season and 58 games for the team since the start of the 2023 season.

Right tackle Jaylon Moore is dealing with an ankle injury so Johnson gives them team experienced depth up front.

VanSumeren has a knee injury. He had five special teams tackles in six games this season.

sports.title: Packers activate Micah Parsons to 53-man roster
sports.summary: Signs continue to point toward Parsons making his 2026 debut against the Rams on Wednesday night.
sports.body:
Green Bay announced on Tuesday that Parsons has been activated to the 53-man roster in advance of Wednesday’s game against the Rams.

Parsons has been medically cleared to play. While he’s officially listed as questionable, all signs point to the edge rusher returning from his torn ACL this week in Los Angeles.

In 14 games for the Packers last year, Parsons tallied 12.5 sacks with 12 tackles for loss and 27 quarterback hits. He also had one pass defensed and two forced fumbles.

Though he wasn’t able to finish the 2025 season, he was still an AP first-team All-Pro for the third time in his career.

Green Bay had an open spot on its 53-man roster, so the club did not need to make a corresponding move.

sports.title: Lions DT Skyler Gill-Howard out for season with knee injury
sports.summary: The Lions have lost another defensive player for the rest of the 2026 season.
sports.body:
Head coach Dan Campbell told reporters on Tuesday that defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard is going to miss the rest of the year. Gill-Howard has a knee injury that will require a surgical repair.

The Lions have also lost defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, linebacker Jimmy Rolder, and linebacker Jack Campbell in recent weeks.

Gill-Howard was a sixth-round pick in April and he appeared in all 10 games for the Lions this season. He had 11 tackles, two sacks, a tackle for loss and six quarterback hits.

sports.title: Kyren Williams off injury report, set to play Wednesday vs. Packers
sports.summary: Rams running back Kyren Williams was listed on the injury report this week with a toe injury, but he is still set to play in Wednesday's game against the Packers.
sports.body:
Williams has no injury designation after he was listed as limited on Sunday. Los Angeles listed him as full on Monday and Tuesday, though the Rams did not practice so Tuesday’s report is an estimate.

Coming off their bye, the Rams treated Monday as a normal Friday and Tuesday as a normal Saturday.

Williams leads the Rams with 616 rushing yards and six touchdowns. He’s also caught 38 passes for 267 yards with a TD.

As expected, L.A. ruled out offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring), offensive lineman Coleman Shelton (hamstring), and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring).

The Rams have no other game statuses. Tight end Davis Allen (oblique), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), linebacker Nate Landman (toe), offensive lineman Justin Dedich (hand), defensive end Kobie Turner (groin), long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), edge rusher Myles Garrett (knee/rest), and quarterback Matthew Stafford (right elbow) are all set to play.

sports.title: Bengals-Commanders clock error brings back memories of Steelers-Chargers clock error in 2015
sports.summary: Monday night's game between the Bengals and Commanders ended with an apparent error by the clock operator.
sports.body:
The Chargers were hosting the Steelers. Here’s the NFL’s official explanation , issued after the game:

“With 2:56 remaining in the fourth quarter, San Diego kicked off to Pittsburgh. The kick resulted in a touchback. By rule, the game clock does not start if the receiving team possesses the ball in the end zone and does not carry it into the field of play.

“Because of an error by the clock operator, the game clock was incorrectly started before the Steelers’ first play from scrimmage following the touchback. That first down snap came with 2:38 left to play instead of 2:56, a difference of 18 seconds.

“The official game time is kept on the stadium scoreboard, but it is the responsibility of the side judge to supervise the timing of the game. Had the side judge or any of the other six on-field officials noticed the timing error, they could have corrected it.

“The game clock is not subject to instant replay review unless there is a timing issue on the last play of the first half or the last play of the game. The performance of the clock operator and game officials will be reviewed per the standard procedure for reviewing every play of every game.”

The Steelers-Chargers situation shows that, when a clock error happens, the side judge becomes responsible for not catching it. On Monday night, that role was filled by Jimmy Buchanan. It was his job to ensure that the clock stopped when it was supposed to stop.

What comes next remains to be seen. In 2015, more than two years before the Supreme Court opened the floodgates for legalized gambling, the NFL interviewed the clock operator and side judge Rob Vernatchi .

The error in the 2015 game didn’t impact the outcome; the Steelers won the game, 24-20. Vernatchi was nevertheless suspended for a week . The NFL thereafter implemented the “ right controls ” to keep it from happening again.

sports.title: Colts sign OT Wanya Morris off Cowboys practice squad
sports.summary: The Colts are adding an offensive lineman.
sports.body:
Wanya Morris is signing with Indianapolis’ 53-man roster off Dallas’ practice squad, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports.

Morris, 26, was traded to the Falcons from the Chiefs in June, but was waived by Atlanta at roster cuts in August. He then joined the Cowboys in early September.

He has not appeared in a regular-season game so far in 2026.

Originally a Kansas City third-round pick, Morris has appeared in 43 career games with 16 starts.

sports.title: Rob Gronkowski, Adrian Peterson, Ben Roethlisberger among players advancing in Hall of Fame voting process
sports.summary: The field will eventually be cut to 13 candidates before the final vote.
sports.body:
The group includes five players who are in their first year of eligibility. They are tight end Rob Gronkowski, running back Adrian Peterson, quarterback Ben Roethlisberger, wide receiver Antonio Brown, and cornerback Richard Sherman.

After changes to the selection process this year, there are no longer Modern and Senior candidates in the player pool. The group of 52 players will be cut to 25 in the next round of voting and then 13 finalists will be selected from that group. They will join Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft in the final pool of eligible candidates with the selection committee selecting a group of between three and seven members.

The full list of players who have advanced to the next round of voting appearsa below.

sports.title: Packers list Micah Parsons, Josh Jacobs as questionable for Wednesday
sports.summary: Micah Parsons has been cleared to make his return from last December's torn ACL, but the Packers didn't make anything certain about the defensive end's status for Wednesday night's game against the Rams on their final injury report.
sports.body:
Parsons is officially listed as questionable after another three days of limited practice participation. The Packers will have to make a roster move to activate Parsons and all signs point to that happening in time for him to face Los Angeles.

Running back Josh Jacobs (finger) was not expected to return this week, but he’s been able to practice the last few days and he also earned a questionable tag for the NFL’s first Thanksgiving Eve game.

Six other Packers are also listed as questionable. They are linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), offensive lineman Travis Glover (shoulder), wide receiver Bo Melton (thigh), wide receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), and guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps).

sports.title: How do you really feel about the Bills playing on Thanksgiving night?
sports.summary: As Thanksgiving Day quickly approaches, fans of the Buffalo Bills have plenty to be thankful for. The team has a 9-1 record and currently sits atop the standings in the AFC. Josh Allen remains and MVP candidate, James Cook is as good as ever, and Gregory Rousseau may be a Defensive Player of the Yea
sports.body: As Thanksgiving Day quickly approaches, fans of the Buffalo Bills have plenty to be thankful for. The team has a 9-1 record and currently sits atop the standings in the AFC. Josh Allen remains and MVP candidate, James Cook is as good as ever, and Gregory Rousseau may be a Defensive Player of the Year candidate. Now the Bills play the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night at Highmark Stadium. To be honest, originally I was excited to see that the Bills were playing on Thanksgiving. It’s is arguably the second greatest football day of the year, behind opening day of the season. The Bills are in the prime-time slot, when all of the hustle and bustle of the holiday has passed, and I can relax that night for the game (at least as much as I can feel relaxed when the Bills play the Chiefs). But now that it is almost Thanksgiving, there is a big part of me that wishes the Bills were not playing on Thursday night. Maybe the matchup with the Chiefs has something to do with it. Playing one of your most hated rivals on a short week never feels right, granted the Bills are not the team that has to travel for the game. I usually find the match-ups with the Chiefs to be more stress-inducing, which might have much to do with this, too. The alternative would be falling asleep in a tryptophan-induced coma by halftime of the prime-time game. That would not be the worst thing, right? So how are you feeling about the Bills playing on Thanksgiving? Is it messing with your travel plans? Are you excited for the game? Will you be making the trip to Highmark Stadium? Be sure to share in the comments below, and I hope that everyone has a Happy Thanksgiving!

sports.body: The time has arrived. An old foe is in their way another time. Kansas City has scored at least 34 points in three straight games, and Buffalo’s defense has not allowed a touchdown since the middle of the Ravens game on Nov. 1. One of those streaks gets tested Thursday night at Highmark Stadium. The Chiefs (8-2) can pull even with the Bills (9-1) and take the head-to-head tiebreaker with a win, so the AFC’s top seed is on the line along with the bragging rights. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills took care of business against an underdog on Sunday, beating the Miami Dolphins. The Jacksonville Jaguars and Cincinnati Bengals both lost to underdogs from the NFC East on Sunday and Monday, which paves the way for the Bills to clinch the number one seed in a new scenario. Yes, with seven games left it is premature to talk about clinching scenarios, but the Bills have a four-game lead in the AFC East plus two games left against the Jets and Dolphins. The division crown is heavily tilted toward the Bills now, and we are starting to look past that to the one seed. (The Bills are obvously focused one game at a time.) With the Jaguars and Bengals losing this week, the Bills now can win the rest of their AFC games and secure the overall record and the AFC record they would need to clinch the one seed, a status that has eluded them throughout Josh Allen’s entire career. Buffalo has games against the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and New England Patriots plus the Dolphins and Jets. Winning those five AFC contests gets them to 14 wins and an 11-1 AFC record with head-to-head tiebreakers over the Broncos and Chiefs. Denver and KC would both have three losses on account of losing to Buffalo. Meanwhile the Jaguars and Bengals could top out at 14-3 but have two AFC losses apiece. Even in a three-way tie scenario, the Bills would come out on top. In short, if the Bills win the rest of their AFC games, they can lose both games to the NFC North’s Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers and still be the one seed in the AFC. sports.body: I think part of being a diehard NFL fan is trying to derive meaning out of everything that happens to a team, no matter how small. Think about the offseason program. How often do we have reports on which players are up and which players are down? These continue into training camp. Then the second half of preseason games produce deep dive analysis of which players are potentially hidden gems or important depth pieces. Every now and then an OTA, training camp, or preseason, breakout turns out to be a preview of a genuine step forward by a developing player. Far more often the players and the hype are forgotten. It also goes this way in late season games when a team has fallen out of the Playoff race. Can a loss help a team secure a high Draft pick to land a franchise changing player? Can a late season surge lead to momentum carrying into a future season and be the first step in instilling a new culture? In both cases the answer is yes. Far more often, however, these games don’t have a ton of meaning either way in the long run. They amount to a bad team playing out the string. The Jets’ Week 11 victory over the Chargers has evoked passions across the fanbase. Some fans are furious about the team hurting its NFL Draft positioning. Others are happy to get the win. I don’t think there’s a “right” or a “wrong” way to be a fan. Everybody wants the same thing in the end, for the Jets to have success. Opinions simply vary on the best way to get there. I can understand fans who are hoping for as high of a pick as possible. Of course, we have seen over and over that the quality of the coaching staff and front office making the pick are generally far more important than where the pick is made. Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, and Lamar Jackson were not the first quarterbacks selected in their respective Draft years. Taking it deeper, one study suggests the odds of the top player drafted at his position having a better career than the third player picked at the same position is only slightly better than a coin toss. Yes, there is the occasional case where losing helps a team land a player who legitimately changes everything, and there are cases where a meaningless late season win causes a team to miss out on that player. Some fans are happy to see their team win for the first time in five weeks. While others are pulling their hair out over what they describe as a frustrating loss to a crappy opponent that screwed up their draft positioning. “A Jets win that feels like a loss to many people in the fan base, and I don’t blame anyone who feels that way because I feel the same way. Watching the Jets go out there and win this game just leaves that sinking feeling in your stomach oh my God they have ruined the tank again. That’s the feeling many in the fan base have, and if you feel that way, you’re not a bad fan because you see the forest through the trees because you understand that a win over a one-win Chargers team could potentially do more damage than good. If you’re going to win games, you want it to be because your young players are playing great, not because 33-year-old Sterling Shepard is scoring two touchdowns on his only two touches of the game,” ESPN New York’s Jake Asman lamented. The Jets were not going to finish 2-15. Anyone who set that expectation set themselves up for failure. They have been in a ton of close games this season. A broken clock is right twice a day. A blind squirrel can find a nut. The Jets were eventually going to stumble into a victory, and who knows if this is the last one. There are still six games left in the 2026 regular season.
